children: shares have lost 24% of their value over the past 30 days, a selloff that BTIG analyst Janine Stichter believes is an unfair punishment for “perceived footwear sector headwinds.”
Accordingly, Stichter initiates coverage of Amer Sports
with a Buy rating and an ambitious $42 price target (51% upside from Wednesday’s close) on several underappreciated factors and 20%+ top-line growth outlook.

“Amer Sports stands out as a multi-brand sportswear platform delivering strong top-line growth near term and low-double-digit to mid-teen percentage growth over the medium term, with each of its brands still relatively early in their growth cycles,” Stichter writes in her note to clients.

strength lies in its brand-autonomous model that enables each brand to run individualized strategies, along with the growth potential for Salomon, and underpenetration of its standout Arc’teryx brand in the U.S. and Europe.
“Having multiple brands growing strongly in tandem is a rarity in retail, and we believe should command a premium,” Stichter says.

has three reportable segments: Technical Apparel, Outdoor Performance, and Ball & Racquet Sports, with each segment represented by popular brands like Arc’teryx, Salomon, and Wilson, respectively. With these brands skewed towards certain regions (Arc’teryx in China, Salomon in EMEA, and Wilson in the Americas), Stichter believes this allows Amer Sports
to create a “customized go-to-market approach tailored to the brand’s specific attributes and consumer engagement needs, rather than being forced into a standardized playbook.”

This strategy translates into lower corporate overhead as a percentage of sales versus other multi-brand peers, as a larger share of expenses are allocated to the individual brand segments versus a shared back end. As a result, Stichter shows that Amer Sports’
corporate expenses as a percentage of sales (4.3%) are the lowest among peers, including VF Corp
“The efficiency of this strategy has been evident in the results. Revenue growth is firing across all segments/brands simultaneously, a rare feat in retail,” Stichter notes.

title: Amer Sports' multiple growth strategy across brands 'a rare feat in retail' -- BTIG
